column2: A hunter's camp has been found above the tree line, with three sky bison calves in a rope pen and a fire built from temple wood. The poachers say the calves were orphaned and that they mean to sell them to a menagerie keeper in the lowlands. The temple's herdsmen want to drive the poachers off. The elders say the Air Nomads do not answer theft with blows.
Buy the calves and send the poachers away.
Have the temple's airbenders drive them off and free the calves.
Ask the local lord to arrest the poachers.

The temple's orchards have caught the leaf-blight. The apples and peaches will not keep, and the temple's stores will not last the winter. The villagers below have grain to spare, but they will not give it away. Their fields were blessed by the temple, and they expect to be paid.
Buy grain at the market price and open the temple stores to the poor.
Ask the villagers for a tithe as their temple's due.
Send the young monks to gather wild roots and nuts in the high pastures.

A rider in dusty armor waits at the temple gate. His lord, a warlord of the eastern valleys, asks for a company of airbenders to carry messages and scout the passes in his war against a rival. He offers silver and a promise of protection. The temple's elders say the Air Nomads have never served a war.
Refuse the demand and send him away empty-handed.
Offer the temple's healers and mediators instead of airbenders.
Send only volunteers, and only as messengers.

A farmer from the western valley has come to the temple with his daughter. The girl can make the dust rise and the shutters rattle when she is angry. The farmer says she has never been taught, and that his wife's grandmother came from the temple. The elders say the girl must be tested, but the farmer says he will not give her up to a life of fasting and temple vows.
Take the girl into the temple and test her.
Leave her with her family and send a monk to teach her.
Refuse her. The temple has no room for a farmer's daughter.

A cracked glider has been found in the temple's oldest store room, wrapped in oiled cloth and marked with the name of an elder who died before the temple's oldest monk was born. The frame is sound, but the wing silk is gone. A young airbender has asked to repair it and fly it on the next clear morning. The elders say the glider belonged to a master and should be left in the dark.
Give the glider to the young airbender to repair.
Have the elders repair it and hang it in the temple hall.
Burn it in the old way and scatter the ashes from the peak.

An old airbender has lived alone on the western peak for thirty years. He comes down once a year for salt and cloth, and the temple's elders say he was once a master of the southern temple. This year he has not come down. A young monk asks leave to climb the peak and look for him, but the elders say the hermit has chosen the wind over the temple.
Send the young monk to climb the peak and bring him down.
Send food and fuel to the peak and leave him be.
Leave him to the wind. The temple has duties enough.
